reported.title: Boost button toggles fan on every press with no rate limit
reported.description: In loop(), when D4 reads LOW the code calls driveFan(true) directly (lines 62-67) with no minimum dwell or toggle-rate limiting, and when the button is released the hysteresis logic can immediately drive the fan back off (lines 87-94). Each press/release cycle therefore produces a fan transition, so repeated presses yield far more than 2 toggles per 5 s: measured 8 toggles in a 5000 ms window for short clean presses, 26 for rapid presses, and 10 for boost chatter. No counter or timestamp enforces the spec's 2-per-5000 ms limit anywhere in the firmware. D5 toggled 8 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.00 s (limit 2), and 8 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

judge_input.spec:
- Temperature probe on A3 at 10 mV/°C; loft fan relay on D5; boost pushbutton on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Turn the fan ON at 36.0 °C or above; turn it OFF at 32.0 °C or below.
- While D4 is held LOW, force the fan ON.
- Fan must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- Print `loft: <temp> C fan=ON` or `loft: <temp> C fan=OFF` every 1000 ms.
- Apply fan changes within 500 ms of a sustained threshold crossing.
